title: M5 P2P eclipse-attack / inbound-sync-DoS red-team adversarial test report
lane: executor-qa-red-team (21-M4RedTeam lineage, extended to p2p connection-layer hardening)
target: p2p/host.go NewHost/NewHostWithConfig (real libp2p host + libp2p.ConnectionManager) and p2p/sync.go registerSyncHandler (real SyncProtocol stream responder + inboundSyncSem) over a genuine libp2p transport -- the same entrypoints every other p2p test in this package drives.
principle: Cases 1-7 (pre-existing, M2) each use exactly one attacker peer and test message/block VALIDITY rejection. Cases 8-9 (this milestone) are genuinely new ground: connection-COUNT and stream-COUNT exhaustion from many simultaneous peers, which nothing in this codebase defended against before this work -- p2p/host.go had no libp2p.ConnectionManager/ConnectionGater/peer-scoring at all (libp2p's own default is unbounded inbound connections), and p2p/sync.go's maxConcurrentSyncs only ever bounded this node's own OUTBOUND catch-up requests, never how many peers could simultaneously open an INBOUND sync stream against it as responder. Per the explicit decision for this milestone (real defenses, not just a documented gap), production code was changed: host.go now attaches a libp2p.ConnectionManager (low=20/high=100, 10s grace period) to every host; gossip.go/sync.go add a per-node inboundSyncSem (cap 8) that Resets excess inbound SyncProtocol streams rather than serving them unboundedly. Both defenses were verified to actually matter (not vacuous) BEFORE being committed: each was temporarily reverted locally and the corresponding new test was confirmed to fail without it, then restored. Both new cases also carry the same liveness requirement cases 1-7 established: after the attack, the honest node must still reach and converge with a genuinely new, honest peer -- not just 'still running', but still able to do the one thing an eclipse/DoS attempt is specifically meant to deny.

adversarial_cases.scenario: connHigh+40 (140) DISTINCT libp2p identities (not reconnects of one identity -- libp2p dedupes those to a single connection, so the attack shape requires genuinely separate peer IDs) each dial the honest host.
adversarial_cases.expected: The connection manager trims total connections down to at most connHigh (100) on its own background schedule (not instantly -- polled up to 90s to account for its grace period). The honest node then still successfully connects to, meshes with, and reaches consensus with a brand-new honest peer.
adversarial_cases.receipt_evidence: CI run https://github.com/ITJHIT/l1chain_JIHO/actions/runs/30558545692 job 90925254072: "adversarial_test.go:603: connections bounded at 20 (limit 100) after 140 sybil attempts" -- --- PASS: TestAdvP2P08EclipseAttemptManySybilPeers (21.03s). Connections settled at the connLow floor (20), not just under the connHigh ceiling (100), i.e. the trim was more aggressive than the minimum bar the test checks for. Liveness (mesh + block convergence with a fresh honest peer) verified within the same test run.

adversarial_cases.scenario: maxConcurrentInboundSyncs*5 (40) sybil peers each open a real SyncProtocol stream against the honest node's responder and hold it open -- never sending the 8-byte start-height the responder blocks reading, never closing it -- the shape of a resource-exhaustion flood against the inbound sync handler.
adversarial_cases.expected: At most maxConcurrentInboundSyncs (8) streams are genuinely accepted/held open by the responder; the rest (>=32) are rejected (Reset) rather than served or queued unboundedly. The honest node stays responsive and still meshes with and converges from a genuinely new peer while the flood is ongoing.
adversarial_cases.receipt_evidence: CI run https://github.com/ITJHIT/l1chain_JIHO/actions/runs/30558545692 job 90925254072: "adversarial_test.go:683: opened 40/40 flood streams", "adversarial_test.go:722: 32/40 flood streams rejected (cap 8)" -- --- PASS: TestAdvP2P09InboundSyncStreamFlood (3.37s). 32/40 rejected is the exact theoretical value (40 - cap 8 = 32): every slot beyond the cap was genuinely rejected, none slipped through. Liveness verified within the same test run.

summary.note: Both new defenses hold under real adversarial load (140 sybil connections trimmed to the connmgr floor; a 40-stream flood rejected down to exactly the 8-stream cap) without sacrificing liveness -- the honest node reaches and converges with a genuine new peer in both cases. IMPLEMENTATION NOTE (process transparency, not a defect in the shipped defense): the first CI run of case 9 failed with only 20/40 streams classified as rejected against a >=32 threshold. This was a test-assertion bug, not a production-code defect -- the classification inferred rejection from Read() latency ('returned under 250ms' = rejected), which raced against CI goroutine-scheduling jitter: a loaded runner can delay the honest side's handler from reaching its s.Reset() call past that narrow window, misclassifying a genuinely-rejected stream as held-open. Fixed by classifying on error TYPE instead of latency, verified against the actual vendored go-yamux/v5 source (const.go): both ErrTimeout and ErrStreamReset are *yamux.Error and satisfy net.Error, but only ErrTimeout has Timeout()==true -- so a net.Error with Timeout()==true can only mean OUR OWN deadline fired (stream genuinely held open), and anything else (including ErrStreamReset) means the remote already reset it. Also switched from sequential per-stream checks with a 500ms deadline to concurrent checks with a 3s deadline, removing the CI-load race entirely. Re-run confirmed the exact expected 32/40. Unlike prior milestones' reports, production_code_modified is true for this milestone by design: the whole point of case 8/9 was to add real defenses, not merely document their absence.
production_code_changes: p2p/host.go: added libp2p.ConnectionManager (connLow=20, connHigh=100, 10s grace period) to every host built by NewHost/NewHostWithConfig -- previously no connection cap of any kind existed.
p2p/gossip.go: added inboundSyncSem (cap maxConcurrentInboundSyncs=8), a resource pool separate from the existing outbound syncSem.
p2p/sync.go: registerSyncHandler's stream callback now acquires inboundSyncSem before any other work, Reset()-ing (not queueing) the stream if the cap is already held -- previously unbounded.
